html:
The Battle of al-Qadisiyyah was fought in about 636 near al-Hira in southern Iraq. An Arab Muslim army under Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas defeated a much larger army of the Sasanian Empire under its general Rostam, who was killed.

The battle lasted several days, and the Persian war elephants at first scattered the Arab horses. Reinforcements from Syria, after the victory at the Yarmuk, helped turn it. The Arabs then crossed the Tigris and took the Sasanian capital Ctesiphon in 637.

It was one of the decisive battles of the Arab conquests: Iraq became a heartland of Islam, and the road into Iran opened, sealed at Nahavand in 642. Saddam Hussein used its name for his war with Iran.
